author: Bobby Grayson
description:
Constructs I decided NOT to support this round, each with the reason.
1. assign_new/3 and update/3 (the other LiveView assigns helpers). assign_new takes a zero-argument fn whose value is only computed when the key is absent -- in the model a record field is always present, so assign_new is always the no-op branch, which is true of a mounted socket but not of one being mounted. Since the lifecycle is not modelled at all, emitting the no-op would be asserting something about mount that the model cannot see. Left blocked.
2. assign with a computed key (assign(socket, key, v) where key is a variable). The state is a record with a fixed set of fields; a computed key needs a real map, which the socket is not here. Left as the unsupported call it is, with a fixture pinning the error.
3. Rebinding the socket inside a callback body (socket = assign(socket, ...), then using it). The whole-state variable has no type in the model to give the let, so the binding fails. A LiveView often writes this; LogsLive does not, so I left it.
4. A Reply inductive for the mixed reply case (see node 722).
title: LiveView constructs left unsupported on purpose
